title: Sherpa Tensing — Camp Eleven: Past Perfect Continuous (B2)
description: Camp eight measures up to now. Camp eleven moves the whole measurement back: an activity that had been running for a while before something else in the…

hero.lede: Camp eight measures up to now. Camp eleven moves the whole measurement back: an activity that had been running for a while before something else in the past happened — and how things looked by the time it did.

cards.head: How long, up to a past moment
cards.body: It had been running for a while before something else in the past happened.
cards.ex: "We had been walking for six hours when we saw the hut."

cards.head: The cause of a past state
cards.body: Why somebody or something was the way you found them.
cards.ex: "His hands were shaking. He had been carrying the pack all day."

cards.head: Repeated, up to that point
cards.body: The same thing over and over, right up to the moment it stopped.
cards.ex: "She had been calling all morning before he answered."

cards.head: Reported speech
cards.body: A present perfect continuous shifts back one step when you report it.
cards.ex: "I've been waiting." → He said he had been waiting.

cards.head: The third conditional
cards.body: An unreal past, with the activity rather than the result in focus.
cards.ex: "If I had been paying attention, I would have seen it."

cards.head: The activity, not the total
cards.body: How the time was filled, rather than what came out of it.

charts.head: Conjugation chart
charts.note: Four pieces, and not one of them changes for the subject. Had is the same for everybody, been never moves, and the -ing form is fixed. This is the easiest tense on the mountain to conjugate and one of the hardest to know when to use.

charts.head: The verbs that refuse the -ing
charts.note: A state is not an activity, so it cannot be in progress. When the meaning is a state, camp ten takes over: had known, never had been knowing.

charts.head: Three mistakes worth naming
charts.note: Almost every error with this tense is one of these three.

head: Not this
This
Why
rows: I was walking for six hours when we arrived.
I had been walking for six hours when we arrived.
A duration measured back from a past moment needs the perfect, not camp six.
I had been knowing him for years.
I had known him for years.
State verbs refuse the continuous, so camp ten takes it.
I had been reading three books.
A number is a result, and results belong to camp ten.

charts.note: Camp ten and camp eleven both sit behind a past moment. The question is only ever which half you are pointing at: the activity that filled the time, or the result that was sitting there when you arrived.

head: Question
Past perfect continuous
Past perfect simple
rows:
The activity and how long it ran.
"He had been painting."

The finished result.
"He had painted the fence."
Never. "He had been writing three emails" is wrong.
Never — know, be, own refuse it.
Always. "He had known her for years."
Measures a duration up to the past moment.
Camp six just says what was going on at it: "I was walking when…"

charts.example: The pair that shows the whole difference: "I was walking when the storm hit" — that is what was going on. "I had been walking for six hours when the storm hit" — that is how long it had been going on for. Camp six gives you the scene; camp eleven gives you the bill.

signals.head: How long it had run
items: all morning / all day / all night

signals.head: The evidence, back then
items: there was paint on his hands
that was why they were late

sections.example: A useful habit: find the past simple first — that is the moment you are standing on. Then ask how long the other thing had already been going when you got there.

diagram.intro: Two brown pegs mark past simple events: the one on the left is where it started, the one on the right is the moment you are measuring to. Between them the trail is the same action happening over and over — faint behind, solid at the head. The purple zone above is what that activity had left by the time you arrived. NOW stands well clear on the right, because none of this reaches it. Click either shape to see it in a sentence.

panels.head: The stretch — how long it had run
items: We had been walking for six hours …

panels.head: The evidence — how things stood then
items: … so the path was under water.
… and he still had not picked up.

quiz.prompt: We _____ for six hours when we finally saw the hut. (walk)
quiz.hint: A duration measured back from a past moment.
quiz.explain: For six hours + a past moment to measure back from: past perfect continuous. Were walking would only say what was going on.

quiz.prompt: His hands were shaking. He _____ the pack all day. (carry)
quiz.explain: The activity came before the shaking hands, and the point is how long it ran. Past perfect continuous.

quiz.prompt: She _____ all morning before he finally answered. (call)
quiz.hint: Repeated, up to a past point.
quiz.explain: Repeated action across a period ending at a past moment takes the past perfect continuous.

quiz.prompt: "I have been waiting an hour." → He said he _____ an hour. (wait)
quiz.hint: Reported speech shifts back one step.
quiz.explain: A present perfect continuous in the original becomes a past perfect continuous when reported.

quiz.prompt: If I _____ attention, I would have seen it. (pay)
quiz.hint: The unreal past, with the activity in focus.
quiz.explain: The third conditional takes if + past perfect; the continuous keeps the focus on the activity rather than a result.

quiz.prompt: I _____ him for years before that evening. (know)
quiz.explain: Know is a state verb and refuses the continuous, so the past perfect simple takes the duration.

quiz.hint: There is a number in the sentence.
quiz.explain: A number is a result, and results belong to the simple. Had been writing would be right without the three.

quiz.prompt: The path was flooded. It _____ all night. (rain)
quiz.hint: The cause of a past state.
quiz.explain: The rain ran up to the moment you found the flooded path, and the duration is the point.

quiz.prompt: How long _____ they _____ before the taxi came? (wait)
quiz.hint: The question this tense was made for.
quiz.explain: How long + had been + -ing is the standard way to ask about a duration ending at a past moment.

quiz.prompt: They _____ well that week, and it showed. (not / sleep)
quiz.explain: Hadn't + been + -ing. The past perfect simple would report it as a finished fact rather than a running condition.

quiz.prompt: I _____ when the phone rang, and I nearly dropped the pan. (cook)
quiz.hint: What was going on, not how long.
quiz.explain: With no duration and no need to measure back, camp six is the right tense: the scene, not the bill.

quiz.prompt: We _____ there for ten years when the mill closed. (live)
quiz.hint: A duration reaching a past event.
quiz.explain: For ten years + a past moment: past perfect continuous. Had lived is also possible, but the continuous keeps the stretch in view.

quiz.prompt: He was covered in mud because he _____ the ditch. (clear)
quiz.explain: The mud is what the activity left behind at that past moment, which is exactly this tense's job.

quiz.prompt: She _____ the same excuse for months before anyone checked. (use)
quiz.explain: Repeated across a period that ends at a past moment takes the past perfect continuous.

results: Clean run. You can hear the difference between what was going on and how long it had been going on.
Solid progress. Worth a look back at camp six and camp ten before camp thirteen.
Good first attempt. The continuous/simple fork is the part to read again.

10: Wir waren schon sechs Stunden unterwegs, als wir die Hütte sahen.
Llevábamos seis horas caminando cuando vimos el refugio.
Nous marchions depuis six heures quand nous avons vu le refuge.
Camminavamo da sei ore quando abbiamo visto il rifugio.
Caminhávamos há seis horas quando vimos o abrigo.
Мы шли уже шесть часов, когда увидели хижину.
كنا نمشي منذ ست ساعات عندما رأينا الكوخ.
我们已经走了六个小时才看到那间小屋。
六時間歩き続けたところで小屋が見えました。
11: Seine Hände zitterten. Er hatte den ganzen Tag den Rucksack getragen.
Le temblaban las manos. Llevaba todo el día cargando la mochila.
Ses mains tremblaient. Il portait le sac depuis le matin.
Gli tremavano le mani. Aveva portato lo zaino tutto il giorno.
As mãos dele tremiam. Tinha carregado a mochila o dia todo.
У него дрожали руки. Он весь день нёс рюкзак.
كانت يداه ترتجفان. كان يحمل الحقيبة طوال اليوم.
他的手在发抖。他背了一整天的包。
手が震えていました。一日中ザックを背負っていたのです。
12: Sie hatte den ganzen Morgen angerufen, bevor er ranging.
Llevaba toda la mañana llamando antes de que él contestara.
Elle appelait depuis le matin avant qu'il ne réponde.
Chiamava da tutta la mattina prima che lui rispondesse.
Ela tinha estado a ligar toda a manhã antes de ele atender.
Она звонила всё утро, прежде чем он ответил.
كانت تتصل طوال الصباح قبل أن يرد.
她打了一早上电话，他才接。
彼が出るまで、彼女は朝からずっと電話をかけていました。
13: „Ich warte schon." → Er sagte, er warte schon eine Weile.
« J'attends depuis un moment. » → Il a dit qu'il attendait depuis un moment.
«Sto aspettando da un po'.» → Ha detto che aspettava da un po'.
«Estou à espera há algum tempo.» → Disse que estava à espera há algum tempo.
«Я жду уже давно.» → Он сказал, что ждал уже давно.
«أنا أنتظر منذ فترة.» ← قال إنه كان ينتظر منذ فترة.
“我已经等了一会儿了。”→ 他说他已经等了一会儿。
「ずっと待っている」→ 彼はずっと待っていたと言いました。
14: Wenn ich aufgepasst hätte, hätte ich es gesehen.
Si hubiera estado prestando atención, lo habría visto.
Si j'avais fait attention, je l'aurais vu.
Se avessi fatto attenzione, l'avrei visto.
Se eu estivesse a prestar atenção, tê-lo-ia visto.
Если бы я был внимателен, я бы это заметил.
如果我当时留意了，就会看到。
注意していたら気づいていたでしょう。
15: Ich hatte es gelesen. (nicht unbedingt zu Ende)
Lo había estado leyendo. (no necesariamente terminado)
我一直在读它。（不一定读完）
それを読んでいました。（読み終えたとは限らない）
16: 他们已经等了好几个小时。
彼らは何時間も待っていました。
17: Es hatte noch nicht lange geregnet.
Il ne pleuvait pas depuis longtemps.
لم تكن تمطر منذ وقت طويل.
雨はまだ降り始めて間もなかった。
18: その前ずっと走っていたのですか。
19: Wie lange waren sie schon gefahren?
Ils conduisaient depuis combien de temps ?
Há quanto tempo estavam a conduzir?
他们已经开了多久的车？
